ESV.1: When David was old and full of days, he made Solomon his son king over Israel.
ESV.2: David  assembled all the leaders of Israel and the priests and the Levites.
ESV.3: The Levites, thirty years old and upward, were numbered, and the total was 38,000 men.
ESV.4: “Twenty-four thousand of these,” David said,  “shall have charge of the work in the house of the LORD, 6,000 shall be officers and judges,
ESV.5: 4,000 gatekeepers, and 4,000 shall offer praises to the LORD with the instruments that I have made for praise.”
ESV.6: And David organized them in divisions corresponding to the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
ESV.7: The sons of Gershon  were Ladan and Shimei.
ESV.8: The sons of Ladan: Jehiel the chief, and Zetham, and Joel, three.
ESV.9: The sons of Shimei: Shelomoth, Haziel, and Haran, three. These were the heads of the fathers' houses of Ladan.
ESV.10: And the sons of Shimei: Jahath, Zina, and Jeush and Beriah. These four were the sons of Shimei.
ESV.11: Jahath was the chief, and Zizah the second; but Jeush and Beriah did not have many sons, therefore they became counted as a single father's house.
ESV.12: The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel, four.
ESV.13: The sons of Amram: Aaron and Moses. Aaron was set apart to dedicate the most holy things, that he and his sons forever should make offerings before the LORD and minister to him and pronounce blessings in his name forever.
ESV.14: But the sons of Moses the man of God were named among the tribe of Levi.
ESV.15: The sons of Moses: Gershom and Eliezer.
ESV.16: The sons of Gershom: Shebuel the chief.
ESV.17: The sons of Eliezer: Rehabiah the chief. Eliezer had no other sons, but the sons of Rehabiah were very many.
ESV.18: The sons of Izhar: Shelomith the chief.
ESV.19: The sons of Hebron: Jeriah the chief, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, and Jekameam the fourth.
ESV.20: The sons of Uzziel: Micah the chief and Isshiah the second.
ESV.21: The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. The sons of Mahli: Eleazar and Kish.
ESV.22: Eleazar died having no sons, but only daughters; their kinsmen, the sons of Kish, married them.
ESV.23: The sons of Mushi: Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth, three.
ESV.24: These were the sons of Levi by their fathers' houses, the heads of fathers' houses as they were listed according to the number of the names of the individuals from twenty years old and upward who were to do the work for the service of the house of the LORD.
ESV.25: For David said, “The LORD, the God of Israel, has given rest to his people, and he dwells in Jerusalem forever.
ESV.26: And so the Levites no longer need to carry the tabernacle or any of the things for its service.”
ESV.27: For by the last words of David the sons of Levi were numbered from twenty years old and upward.
ESV.28: For their duty was to assist the sons of Aaron for the service of the house of the LORD, having the care of the courts and the chambers, the cleansing of all that is holy, and any work for the service of the house of God.
ESV.29: Their duty was also to assist with the showbread, the flour for the grain offering, the wafers of unleavened bread, the baked offering, the offering mixed with oil, and all measures of quantity or size.
ESV.30: And they were to stand every morning, thanking and praising the LORD, and likewise at evening,
ESV.31: and whenever burnt offerings were offered to the LORD on Sabbaths, new moons, and feast days, according to the number required of them, regularly before the LORD.
ESV.32: Thus they were to keep charge of the tent of meeting and the sanctuary, and to attend the sons of Aaron, their brothers, for the service of the house of the LORD.

NKJV.1: So when David was old and full of days, he made his son Solomon king over Israel.
NKJV.2: And he gathered together all the leaders of Israel, with the priests and the Levites.
NKJV.3: Now the Levites were numbered from the age of thirty years and above; and the number of individual males was thirty-eight thousand.
NKJV.4: Of these, twenty-four thousand were to look after the work of the house of the LORD, six thousand were officers and judges,
NKJV.5: four thousand were gatekeepers, and four thousand praised the LORD with musical instruments, “which I made,” said David, “for giving praise.”
NKJV.6: Also David separated them into divisions among the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
NKJV.7: Of the Gershonites: Laadan and Shimei.
NKJV.8: The sons of Laadan: the first Jehiel, then Zetham and Joel—three in all.
NKJV.9: The sons of Shimei: Shelomith, Haziel, and Haran—three in all. These were the heads of the fathers’ houses of Laadan.
NKJV.10: And the sons of Shimei: Jahath, Zina, Jeush, and Beriah. These were the four sons of Shimei.
NKJV.11: Jahath was the first and Zizah the second. But Jeush and Beriah did not have many sons; therefore they were assigned as one father’s house.
NKJV.12: The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel—four in all.
NKJV.13: The sons of Amram: Aaron and Moses; and Aaron was set apart, he and his sons forever, that he should sanctify the most holy things, to burn incense before the LORD, to minister to Him, and to give the blessing in His name forever.
NKJV.14: Now the sons of Moses the man of God were reckoned to the tribe of Levi.
NKJV.15: The sons of Moses were Gershon and Eliezer.
NKJV.16: Of the sons of Gershon, Shebuel was the first.
NKJV.17: Of the descendants of Eliezer, Rehabiah was the first. And Eliezer had no other sons, but the sons of Rehabiah were very many.
NKJV.18: Of the sons of Izhar, Shelomith was the first.
NKJV.19: Of the sons of Hebron, Jeriah was the first, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, and Jekameam the fourth.
NKJV.20: Of the sons of Uzziel, Michah was the first and Jesshiah the second.
NKJV.21: The sons of Merari were Mahli and Mushi. The sons of Mahli were Eleazar and Kish.
NKJV.22: And Eleazar died, and had no sons, but only daughters; and their brethren, the sons of Kish, took them as wives.
NKJV.23: The sons of Mushi were Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth—three in all.
NKJV.24: These were the sons of Levi by their fathers’ houses—the heads of the fathers’ houses as they were counted individually by the number of their names, who did the work for the service of the house of the LORD, from the age of twenty years and above.
NKJV.25: For David said, “The LORD God of Israel has given rest to His people, that they may dwell in Jerusalem forever”;
NKJV.26: and also to the Levites, “They shall no longer carry the tabernacle, or any of the articles for its service.”
NKJV.27: For by the last words of David the Levites were numbered from twenty years old and above;
NKJV.28: because their duty was to help the sons of Aaron in the service of the house of the LORD, in the courts and in the chambers, in the purifying of all holy things and the work of the service of the house of God,
NKJV.29: both with the showbread and the fine flour for the grain offering, with the unleavened cakes and what is baked in the pan, with what is mixed and with all kinds of measures and sizes;
NKJV.30: to stand every morning to thank and praise the LORD, and likewise at evening;
NKJV.31: and at every presentation of a burnt offering to the LORD on the Sabbaths and on the New Moons and on the set feasts, by number according to the ordinance governing them, regularly before the LORD;
NKJV.32: and that they should attend to the needs of the tabernacle of meeting, the needs of the holy place, and the needs of the sons of Aaron their brethren in the work of the house of the LORD.

NASB.1: Now when David reached old age, he made his son Solomon king over Israel.
NASB.2: And he gathered together all the leaders of Israel with the priests and the Levites.
NASB.3: The Levites were numbered from thirty years old and upward, and their number by census of men was 38,000.
NASB.4: Of these, 24,000 were to oversee the work of the house of the LORD; and 6,000 [were] officers and judges,
NASB.5: and 4,000 [were] gatekeepers, and 4,000 [were] praising the LORD with the instruments which David made for giving praise.
NASB.6: David divided them into divisions according to the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
NASB.7: Of the Gershonites [were] Ladan and Shimei.
NASB.8: The sons of Ladan [were] Jehiel the first and Zetham and Joel, three.
NASB.9: The sons of Shimei [were] Shelomoth and Haziel and Haran, three. These were the heads of the fathers' [households] of Ladan.
NASB.10: The sons of Shimei [were] Jahath, Zina, Jeush and Beriah. These four [were] the sons of Shimei.
NASB.11: Jahath was the first and Zizah the second; but Jeush and Beriah did not have many sons, so they became a father's household, one class.
NASB.12: The sons of Kohath were four: Amram, Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel.
NASB.13: The sons of Amram were Aaron and Moses. And Aaron was set apart to sanctify him as most holy, he and his sons forever, to burn incense before the LORD, to minister to Him and to bless in His name forever.
NASB.14: But [as for] Moses the man of God, his sons were named among the tribe of Levi.
NASB.15: The sons of Moses [were] Gershom and Eliezer.
NASB.16: The son of Gershom [was] Shebuel the chief.
NASB.17: The son of Eliezer was Rehabiah the chief; and Eliezer had no other sons, but the sons of Rehabiah were very many.
NASB.18: The son of Izhar was Shelomith the chief.
NASB.19: The sons of Hebron [were] Jeriah the first, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third and Jekameam the fourth.
NASB.20: The sons of Uzziel [were] Micah the first and Isshiah the second.
NASB.21: The sons of Merari were Mahli and Mushi. The sons of Mahli [were] Eleazar and Kish.
NASB.22: Eleazar died and had no sons, but daughters only, so their brothers, the sons of Kish, took them [as wives].
NASB.23: The sons of Mushi [were] three: Mahli, Eder and Jeremoth.
NASB.24: These were the sons of Levi according to their fathers' households, [even] the heads of the fathers' [households] of those of them who were counted, in the number of names by their census, doing the work for the service of the house of the LORD, from twenty years old and upward.
NASB.25: For David said, 'The LORD God of Israel has given rest to His people, and He dwells in Jerusalem forever.
NASB.26: 'Also, the Levites will no longer need to carry the tabernacle and all its utensils for its service.'
NASB.27: For by the last words of David the sons of Levi [were] numbered from twenty years old and upward.
NASB.28: For their office is to assist the sons of Aaron with the service of the house of the LORD, in the courts and in the chambers and in the purifying of all holy things, even the work of the service of the house of God,
NASB.29: and with the showbread, and the fine flour for a grain offering, and unleavened wafers, or [what is baked in] the pan or what is well-mixed, and all measures of volume and size.
NASB.30: They are to stand every morning to thank and to praise the LORD, and likewise at evening,
NASB.31: and to offer all burnt offerings to the LORD, on the sabbaths, the new moons and the fixed festivals in the number [set] by the ordinance concerning them, continually before the LORD.
NASB.32: Thus they are to keep charge of the tent of meeting, and charge of the holy place, and charge of the sons of Aaron their relatives, for the service of the house of the LORD.

NLT.1: When David was an old man, he appointed his son Solomon to be king over Israel.
NLT.2: David summoned all the leaders of Israel, together with the priests and Levites.
NLT.3: All the Levites who were thirty years old or older were counted, and the total came to 38,000.
NLT.4: Then David said, “From all the Levites, 24,000 will supervise the work at the Temple of the LORD. Another 6,000 will serve as officials and judges.
NLT.5: Another 4,000 will work as gatekeepers, and 4,000 will praise the LORD with the musical instruments I have made.”
NLT.6: Then David divided the Levites into divisions named after the clans descended from the three sons of Levi — Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
NLT.7: The Gershonite family units were defined by their lines of descent from Libni and Shimei, the sons of Gershon.
NLT.8: Three of the descendants of Libni were Jehiel (the family leader), Zetham, and Joel.
NLT.9: These were the leaders of the family of Libni. Three of the descendants of Shimei were Shelomoth, Haziel, and Haran.
NLT.10: Four other descendants of Shimei were Jahath, Ziza, Jeush, and Beriah.
NLT.11: Jahath was the family leader, and Ziza was next. Jeush and Beriah were counted as a single family because neither had many sons.
NLT.12: Four of the descendants of Kohath were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
NLT.13: The sons of Amram were Aaron and Moses. Aaron and his descendants were set apart to dedicate the most holy things, to offer sacrifices in the LORD’s presence, to serve the LORD, and to pronounce blessings in his name forever.
NLT.14: As for Moses, the man of God, his sons were included with the tribe of Levi.
NLT.15: The sons of Moses were Gershom and Eliezer.
NLT.16: The descendants of Gershom included Shebuel, the family leader.
NLT.17: Eliezer had only one son, Rehabiah, the family leader. Rehabiah had numerous descendants.
NLT.18: The descendants of Izhar included Shelomith, the family leader.
NLT.19: The descendants of Hebron included Jeriah (the family leader), Amariah (the second), Jahaziel (the third), and Jekameam (the fourth).
NLT.20: The descendants of Uzziel included Micah (the family leader) and Isshiah (the second).
NLT.21: The descendants of Merari included Mahli and Mushi. The sons of Mahli were Eleazar and Kish.
NLT.22: Eleazar died with no sons, only daughters. His daughters married their cousins, the sons of Kish.
NLT.23: Three of the descendants of Mushi were Mahli, Eder, and Jerimoth.
NLT.24: These were the descendants of Levi by clans, the leaders of their family groups, registered carefully by name. Each had to be twenty years old or older to qualify for service in the house of the LORD.
NLT.25: For David said, “The LORD, the God of Israel, has given us peace, and he will always live in Jerusalem.
NLT.26: Now the Levites will no longer need to carry the Tabernacle and its furnishings from place to place.”
NLT.27: In accordance with David’s final instructions, all the Levites twenty years old or older were registered for service.
NLT.28: The work of the Levites was to assist the priests, the descendants of Aaron, as they served at the house of the LORD. They also took care of the courtyards and side rooms, helped perform the ceremonies of purification, and served in many other ways in the house of God.
NLT.29: They were in charge of the sacred bread that was set out on the table, the choice flour for the grain offerings, the wafers made without yeast, the cakes cooked in olive oil, and the other mixed breads. They were also responsible to check all the weights and measures.
NLT.30: And each morning and evening they stood before the LORD to sing songs of thanks and praise to him.
NLT.31: They assisted with the burnt offerings that were presented to the LORD on Sabbath days, at new moon celebrations, and at all the appointed festivals. The required number of Levites served in the LORD’s presence at all times, following all the procedures they had been given.
NLT.32: And so, under the supervision of the priests, the Levites watched over the Tabernacle and the Temple and faithfully carried out their duties of service at the house of the LORD.

WEB.2: He gathered together all the princes of Israel, with the priests and the Levites.
WEB.3: The Levites were counted from thirty years old and upward; and their number by their polls, man by man, was thirty-eight thousand.
WEB.4: David said, “Of these, twenty-four thousand were to oversee the work of Yahweh’s house, six thousand were officers and judges,
WEB.5: four thousand were doorkeepers, and four thousand praised Yahweh with the instruments which I made for giving praise.”
WEB.6: David divided them into divisions according to the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
WEB.7: Of the Gershonites: Ladan and Shimei.
WEB.8: The sons of Ladan: Jehiel the chief, Zetham, and Joel, three.
WEB.9: The sons of Shimei: Shelomoth, Haziel, and Haran, three. These were the heads of the fathers’ households of Ladan.
WEB.10: The sons of Shimei: Jahath, Zina, Jeush, and Beriah. These four were the sons of Shimei.
WEB.11: Jahath was the chief, and Zizah the second; but Jeush and Beriah didn’t have many sons; therefore they became a fathers’ house in one reckoning.
WEB.12: The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel, four.
WEB.13: The sons of Amram: Aaron and Moses; and Aaron was separated, that he should sanctify the most holy things, he and his sons, forever, to burn incense before Yahweh, to minister to him, and to bless in his name, forever.
WEB.14: But as for Moses the man of God, his sons were named among the tribe of Levi.
WEB.15: The sons of Moses: Gershom and Eliezer.
WEB.16: The sons of Gershom: Shebuel the chief.
WEB.17: The sons of Eliezer were: Rehabiah the chief; and Eliezer had no other sons; but the sons of Rehabiah were very many.
WEB.18: The sons of Izhar: Shelomith the chief.
WEB.19: The sons of Hebron: Jeriah the chief, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, and Jekameam the fourth.
WEB.20: The sons of Uzziel: Micah the chief, and Isshiah the second.
WEB.21: The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. The sons of Mahli: Eleazar and Kish.
WEB.22: Eleazar died, and had no sons, but daughters only: and their brothers the sons of Kish took them as wives.
WEB.23: The sons of Mushi: Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth, three.
WEB.24: These were the sons of Levi after their fathers’ houses, even the heads of the fathers’ houses of those who were counted individually, in the number of names by their polls, who did the work for the service of Yahweh’s house, from twenty years old and upward.
WEB.25: For David said, “Yahweh, the God of Israel, has given rest to his people; and he dwells in Jerusalem forever.
WEB.26: Also the Levites will no longer need to carry the tabernacle and all its vessels for its service.”
WEB.27: For by the last words of David the sons of Levi were counted, from twenty years old and upward.
WEB.28: For their office was to wait on the sons of Aaron for the service of Yahweh’s house, in the courts, and in the rooms, and in the purifying of all holy things, even the work of the service of God’s house;
WEB.29: for the show bread also, and for the fine flour for a meal offering, whether of unleavened wafers, or of that which is baked in the pan, or of that which is soaked, and for all measurements of quantity and size;
WEB.30: and to stand every morning to thank and praise Yahweh, and likewise in the evening;
WEB.31: and to offer all burnt offerings to Yahweh, on the Sabbaths, on the new moons, and on the set feasts, in number according to the ordinance concerning them, continually before Yahweh;
WEB.32: and that they should keep the duty of the Tent of Meeting, the duty of the holy place, and the duty of the sons of Aaron their brothers, for the service of Yahweh’s house.

CSB17.1: When David was old and full of days, <sup>ⓗ</sup> he installed his son Solomon as king over Israel. <sup>ⓘ</sup>
CSB17.2: Then he gathered all the leaders of Israel, the priests, and the Levites.
CSB17.3: The Levites thirty years old or more were counted; <sup>ⓙ</sup> the total number of men was thirty-eight thousand by headcount. <sup>ⓚ</sup>
CSB17.4: “Of these,” David said, “twenty-four thousand are to be in charge of the work on the LORD’s temple, <sup>ⓛ</sup> six thousand are to be officers and judges, <sup>ⓜ</sup>
CSB17.5: four thousand are to be gatekeepers, and four thousand are to praise the LORD with the instruments that I have made for worship.” <sup>ⓝ</sup>
CSB17.6: Then David divided them into divisions according to Levi’s sons: <sup>ⓐ</sup> Gershom, <sup>[1]</sup> Kohath, and Merari.
CSB17.8: Ladan’s sons: Jehiel was the first, then Zetham, and Joel — three.
CSB17.9: Shimei’s sons: Shelomoth, Haziel, and Haran — three. Those were the heads of the families of Ladan.
CSB17.10: Shimei’s sons: Jahath, Zizah, [2] Jeush, and Beriah. Those were Shimei’s sons — four.
CSB17.11: Jahath was the first and Zizah was the second; however, Jeush and Beriah did not have many sons, so they became one family [3] and received a single assignment.
CSB17.12: Kohath’s sons: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel — four.
CSB17.13:
Amram’s sons: ⓑ Aaron and Moses.
Aaron, along with his descendants, ⓒ was set apart forever to consecrate the most holy things, to burn incense in the presence of the LORD, ⓓ to minister to him, and to pronounce blessings in his name forever.
CSB17.14: As for Moses the man of God, <sup>ⓔ</sup> his sons were named among the tribe of Levi.
CSB17.17: Eliezer’s sons were Rehabiah, first; Eliezer did not have any other sons, but Rehabiah’s sons were very numerous.
CSB17.19: Hebron’s sons: Jeriah was first, Amariah second, Jahaziel third, and Jekameam fourth.
CSB17.20: Uzziel’s sons: Micah was first, and Isshiah second.
CSB17.21: Merari’s sons: Mahli and Mushi. Mahli’s sons: Eleazar and Kish.
CSB17.22: Eleazar died having no sons, only daughters. Their cousins, the sons of Kish, married them.
CSB17.23: Mushi’s sons: Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth — three.
CSB17.24: These were the descendants of Levi by their ancestral families <sup>[4]</sup>  — the family heads, according to their registration by name in the headcount — twenty years old or more, who worked in the service of the LORD’s temple. <sup>ⓕ</sup>
CSB17.25: For David said, “The LORD God of Israel has given rest to his people, <sup>ⓖ</sup> and he has come to stay in Jerusalem forever.
CSB17.26: Also, the Levites no longer need to carry the tabernacle or any of the equipment for its service” <sup>ⓗ</sup>  —
CSB17.27: for according to the last words of David, the Levites twenty years old or more were to be counted —
CSB17.28: “but their duty will be to assist the descendants of Aaron with the service of the LORD’s temple, being responsible for the courts and the chambers, the purification of all the holy things, and the work of the service of God’s temple —
CSB17.29: as well as the rows of the Bread of the Presence, <sup>ⓘ</sup> the fine flour for the grain offering, <sup>ⓙ</sup> the wafers of unleavened bread, the baking, <sup>[5]</sup> <sup>ⓚ</sup> the mixing, <sup>ⓛ</sup> and all measurements of volume and length. <sup>ⓜ</sup>
CSB17.30: They are also to stand every morning to give thanks and praise to the LORD, and likewise in the evening.
CSB17.31: Whenever burnt offerings are offered to the LORD on the Sabbaths, New Moons, <sup>ⓝ</sup> and appointed festivals, they are to offer them regularly in the LORD’s presence according to the number prescribed for them. <sup>ⓐ</sup>
CSB17.32: They are to carry out their responsibilities for the tent of meeting, for the holy place, <sup>ⓑ</sup> and for their relatives, the descendants of Aaron, <sup>ⓒ</sup> in the service of the LORD’s temple.”

AMP.1: When David reached old age, he made his son Solomon king over Israel.
AMP.2: And he assembled together all the leaders of Israel with the priests and Levites.
AMP.3: The Levites thirty years old and upward were counted, and their number man by man was 38,000.
AMP.4: Of these24,000 were to oversee and inspect the work of the house of the LORD and 6,000 were to be administrators and judges,
AMP.5: and 4,000 were gatekeepers, and 4,000 [musicians] were to praise the LORD with the instruments which David made for giving praise.
AMP.6: And David organized them into divisions according to the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
AMP.7: Of the Gershonites: Ladan (Libni) and Shimei.
AMP.8: The sons of Ladan: Jehiel the first and Zetham and Joel—three in all.
AMP.9: The sons of Shimei: Shelomoth, Haziel, and Haran—three in all. These were the heads of the fathers' households of Ladan.
AMP.10: The sons of Shimei: Jahath, Zina (Zizah), Jeush, and Beriah. These were the four sons of Shimei.
AMP.11: Jahath was the first and Zizah the second; but Jeush and Beriah did not have many sons [not enough for a father's house or clan], so they were [counted together] as one father's household, one working group.
AMP.12: The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel—four in all.
AMP.13: The sons of Amram: Aaron and Moses. Aaron was set apart to consecrate him as most holy, he and his sons forever, to burn incense before the LORD, attend to His service, and to bless [worshipers] in His name forever.
AMP.14: But as for Moses the man of God, his sons were counted among the tribe of Levi.
AMP.15: The sons of Moses: Gershom and Eliezer.
AMP.16: The son of Gershom: Shebuel the chief.
AMP.17: The son of Eliezer was Rehabiah the chief. Eliezer had no other sons, but Rehabiah's sons were very many [in number].
AMP.18: The son of Izhar: Shelomith the chief.
AMP.19: The sons of Hebron: Jeriah the first, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, and Jekameam the fourth.
AMP.20: The sons of Uzziel: Micah the first and Isshiah the second.
AMP.21: The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. The sons of Mahli: Eleazar and Kish.
AMP.22: Eleazar died and had no sons, but daughters only, and their relatives, the sons of Kish, took them as wives.
AMP.23: The sons of Mushi: Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth—three in all.
AMP.24: These were the Levites by their fathers' households, the heads of the fathers' households of those registered, according to the number of names of the individuals who were the servants of the house of the LORD, from twenty years old and upward.
AMP.25: For David said, "The LORD God of Israel, has given peace and rest to His people, and He dwells in Jerusalem forever.
AMP.26: Also, the Levites will no longer need to carry the tabernacle and all its utensils for its service."
AMP.27: For by the last words of David, the Levites from twenty years old and above were counted.
AMP.28: For their duty is to assist [the priests] the sons of Aaron in the service of the house of the LORD, in [caring for] the courtyards, the chambers, the purifying of all holy things, and any work of the service of the house of God,
AMP.29: and with the showbread, and the fine flour for a grain offering, and unleavened wafers, or what is baked in the pan or what is well-mixed, and all measures of volume and size [as the Law of Moses required].
AMP.30: They are to stand every morning to thank and praise the LORD, and likewise at evening,
AMP.31: and to offer all burnt sacrifices to the LORD on the Sabbaths, the new moons, and the festivals by number according to the ordinance concerning them, continually before the LORD.
AMP.32: So they shall be responsible for the Tent of Meeting, the Holy Place, and the sons of Aaron their relatives, for the service of the house of the LORD.

MSG.1: When David got to be an old man, he made his son Solomon king over Israel.
MSG.2: At the same time he brought together all the leaders of Israel, the priests, and the Levites.
MSG.3: The Levites thirty years and older were counted; the total was 38,000.
MSG.4: David sorted them into work groups: "24,000 are in charge of administering worship in the sanctuary; 6,000 are officials and judges;
MSG.5: 4,000 are security guards; and 4,000 are to serve in the orchestra, praising God with instruments that I have provided for praise."
MSG.6: David then divided the Levites into groupings named after the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
MSG.8: The three sons of Ladan: Jehiel, Zetham, and Joel.
MSG.9: The three sons of Shimei: Shelomoth, Haziel, and Haran, all heads of the families of Ladan.
MSG.10: The four sons of Shimei: Jahath, Ziza, Jeush, and Beriah.
MSG.11: Jahath came first, followed by Ziza. Jeush and Beriah did not have many sons so they were counted as one family with one task.
MSG.12: The four sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
MSG.13: The sons of Amram: Aaron and Moses. Aaron was especially ordained to work in the Holy of Holies, to burn incense before God, to serve God and bless his Name always. This was a permanent appointment for Aaron and his sons.
MSG.14: Moses and his sons were counted in the tribe of Levi.
MSG.15: The sons of Moses: Gershom and Eliezer.
MSG.16: Shubael was the first son of Gershom.
MSG.17: Rehabiah was the first and only son of Eliezer; but though Eliezer had no other sons, Rehabiah had many sons.
MSG.18: Shelomith was the first son of Izhar.
MSG.19: Hebron had four sons: Jeriah, Amariah, Jahaziel, and Jekameam.
MSG.20: Uzziel had two sons: Micah and Isshiah.
MSG.21: The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. The sons of Mahli: Eleazar and Kish.
MSG.22: Eleazar died without any sons, only daughters. Their cousins, the sons of Kish, married the daughters.
MSG.23: Mushi had three sons: Mahli, Eder, and Jerimoth.
MSG.24: These are the sons of Levi twenty years and older, divided up according to families and heads of families and listed in the work groups that took care of the worship in the sanctuary of God.
MSG.25: David said, "Now that the God of Israel has given rest to his people and made Jerusalem his permanent home,
MSG.26: the Levites no longer have to carry the Tabernacle and all the furniture required for the work of worship."
MSG.27: These last words of David referred only to Levites twenty years old and above.
MSG.28: From now on the assigned work of the Levites was to assist Aaron's sons in the work of worship in God's house: maintain courtyards and closets, keep the furniture and utensils of worship clean, take care of any extra work needed in the work of worship,
MSG.29: and provide bread for the table and flour for the Meal Offerings and the unraised wafers—all baking and mixing, all measuring and weighing.
MSG.30: Also they were to be present for morning prayers, thanking and praising God, for evening prayers,
MSG.31: and at the service of Whole-Burnt-Offerings to God on Sabbath, at New Moons, and at all festivals. They were on regular duty to serve God according to their assignment and the required number.
MSG.32: In short, the Levites, with the sons of Aaron as their companions in the ministry of holy worship, were responsible for everything that had to do with worship: the place and times and ordering of worship.
